I recomputed by hand against the code: V3.riverDistance (capsule per leg, r = max(w)/2), liquidDistance, nearBridge/onBridge (2D, no height check), layLiquid (joint drum w/2, skipped when depth â‰¤ 0.01), layBridge (the deck at B.deck raises with no code change; side ramps only when there are gaps), Raft.area/shift/step (DOCK_SPEED compares the raft's own speed through the water; Raft.new clamps homeDock to 1 or 2), Current.flow (no bridge awareness), Cookie.triggers (FEET_SLACK against floorTop + B.deck, so waders under a raised deck never trigger), Flyers hiveSpotOk (no liquid rule) and Nests_Test CH1/CE1 plus Layout_Test CH3.

All three raised-bridge mechanisms are feasible: underside clearance is 9.1 (A), 8.1 (B) and 8.6 (C) against a raft top of about 6.8; SINK exceeds deck + 0.4 in each; the decks cover the wet spans when recomputed.

The test failures I found:
- A and C both fail Nests_Test CH1's rule that every pair of posts is at least 30 apart. A: candyPostC13 vs candyPostR6, 27.7. C: the same pair at 18.5, and candyPostC8 vs candyPostR6 at 29.5.
- A and C both fail the Layout_Test CH3 and CH1 syrup rules against the legacy Layout.LAKE discs (C6, C10 and candyPostC6 moved into the old syrup zone).
- Neither checker models those rules (I confirmed this by grepping geo.ps1 and Geo.cs), so their '0 failures' claims are wrong.
- B's checker covers the full CH1 rule set, and I found no failing rule.
- B's defects are gameplay and visual rather than test failures: a 5-stud barrier leak behind the lake, the open west-edge mouth (visible, and an easy bypass from the hub side), no rule keeping hives off the chocolate, and the M1 drum slip.

A also gives up the owner's GT 'cake at the end' rule and the river's barrier role. That is why it ranks last even though it moves the least.

C has the strongest mechanisms (basins, the raftBlocks fallback, flood fills, the layAll relay, RESTORE), and grafting them onto B gives the best result.
